overview: This Senate resolution marks the tenth anniversary of the June 23, 2016, floods in West Virginia, when heavy storms caused flash flooding that killed 23 people. It recalls the widespread damage, including destroyed homes, schools, roads and bridges and power outages for more than half a million people, and the federal disaster declaration that followed. It honors those who died and those affected, and praises first responders and neighbors who helped and the communities that rebuilt. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on July 15, 2026.
for: Supporters say it honors the victims and recognizes the resilience of West Virginia communities that rebuilt after the disaster.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
